content:
mira: Heads-up — nightly CI (master) popped a small-batch p95 tail this run (build 0f3a2b). p95 jumped ~120ms -> ~360ms on the 4096-token workload. Noticed around 01:10 UTC. @kai @devon can someone pick this up for the night?

kai: I'll take a first pass. Any repro steps or the job id?

mira: Nightly job id: nightly-ci-20260317-01. Repro command we use locally:
```bash
./run_bench --model zora-13b --batch-size 4 --tokens 4096 --seed 42 --profile /tmp/profile.pb
```
Perf dashboard: https://perf.redwood.dev/dashboards/nightly/0f3a2b (private link)

ops-bot: Alert: nightly-ci failed check: tail-latency > threshold (360ms) for job nightly-ci-20260317-01. Artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-nightly/0f3a2b/

devon: Quick glance at the logs, seeing repeated KV_CACHE_EVICT entries around the spike:
```
[01:09:58] kv_cache: evicting 32 entries (current size 124MB)
[01:10:00] kv_cache: refill triggered, refill_time=48ms
[01:10:01] scheduler: stall detected, gpu_wait=212ms
```
Not 100% sure but this pattern lines up with previous small-batch tails.

kai: Running the local repro now with --trace-kv. If the eviction/refill is the culprit we should see increased refill_time in the profile. Sharing profile tar when done. :eyes:

sam: I'm on-call tonight. If it looks like an infra scheduling issue we can flip the fallback model variant to small-batch-v0.2 to keep SLOs while we investigate. Need a +1 to proceed if we can't stabilize before 02:15 UTC.

mira: Good plan. If we do a fallback, let's also start an automated bisect across the recent PR window that touched batching/kv-cache. Suspect range: PRs #3421..#3440 (roughly last 10 merges).

devon: I'll kick off a focused bisect job on a small cluster. Repro helper script (run inside container):
```python
# repro_helper.py
import subprocess
cmd = ['./run_bench','--model','zora-13b','--batch-size','4','--tokens','4096']
print(subprocess.check_output(cmd))
```
Drop results to s3 under s3://redwood-nightly/bisect/3591234567/ so we can inspect traces.

kai: Local profile uploaded: https://perf.redwood.dev/profiles/3591234567/profile.pb.gz
Initial observation: kernel scheduling stalls (~180-220ms) correlated with large memcpy calls. Could be cushion allocator or memcpy path regressed after the quantization patch (PR #3434).

mira: If bisect points to #3434, we should default rollback + patch for the memcpy path. But let's wait for the bisect. Sam, are you okay to toggle fallback if we don't have a fix?

sam: Yep. I'll hold until 02:15 UTC then flip to small-batch-v0.2 and annotate the rollback in the release notes. Will also create a P0 ticket and assign to @kai + @devon for follow-up tomorrow.

devon: Kicked off bisect job (job id bisect-3591234). ETA ~45m. I uploaded the initial log bundle and a minimal trace to s3://redwood-nightly/bisect/3591234567/logs.tar.gz

kai: Thanks. If bisect lands on #3434 ping me directly, I'll stage a hotfix for the memcpy path. Otherwise I'll keep digging through kernel traces and memcopy timelines.

mira: Thanks everyone. Ping here with any high-level updates. I'll put a short status note in the morning. For handoff, drop artifacts and a one-line summary in the bisect folder.

sam: ack :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Handoff reminder scheduled at 02:30 UTC for unresolved issues in job nightly-ci-20260317-01.

mira: Closing loop — if anyone finds a fast mitigation, post the exact commands here so I can approve the rollback quickly.

kai: Will do.
